title: NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs
subtitle: Consumer NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs carried the Inference Fabric, the capabilities model and early ActiveKV work, first on one card and then on two mismatched cards draining one broker queue.

stats.label: tokens a second held for ten hours on one card

to build the shared TensorRT-LLM image from source

lede: I have run consumer Blackwell GPUs hard in five roles: bulk generation, a co-resident custom decoder, real-time speech, provisioned compute and early cache-offload work. In each I measured what the card does and built to that; cache windows, memory left beside a resident model and utilisation all come from the card. Inference Fabric asked how much of a consumer Blackwell GPU's real throughput a disciplined serving design could reach on bulk generation. On one 32 GB card the 7-billion-parameter dense model ran in FP8. Then a second, smaller 16 GB Blackwell GPU joined it, both draining one backlog.
quote: Mismatched cards are where a plain queue breaks down.
evidence: NVIDIA Blackwell development: TensorRT-LLM built from source for compute capability 12.0 and kernels compiled with CUDA 13.1 as native SM 120 binaries, other GPUs refused at runtime.
High-throughput batch inference: one 32 GB card at 96.9% streaming-multiprocessor utilisation, holding ~65,000 tokens a second for ten hours through 4.95M tasks with zero retries.
Heterogeneous GPU scheduling: a 32 GB and a 16 GB card on one broker queue, each described by four integers, reaching a five-minute mean of 163,000 tokens a second.
GPU memory co-residency: a router engine in 2,740 MiB beside a resident model of about 30B, serving a burst of 2,048 simultaneous clients with none rejected or corrupted.
author: Corey James
